title: disclosed classification rules
description: How a value is absent, which is not the same as what the value is. Five states: a credible reported value, a disclosed value outside its credible range, a value withheld on purpose, a question that does not apply, and a gap with no stated reason. Rendered naively the last four all become 0, and a reader cannot tell a college that admits nobody from a college that declined to say.

version.description: Version of this rule-file format, not of the disclosed package.

rules.description: One entry per column to classify.

disclosure.title: disclosure state
disclosure.description: The five states. There is no sixth.

column.description: Column header in the CSV being classified.

credible_min.description: Inclusive lower bound of the credible range; null disables it.

credible_max.description: Inclusive upper bound of the credible range; null disables it.

zero_is_credible.description: Whether an exact zero is a believable measurement here. False for rates and prices, where zero is nearly always a reporting artifact.

sentinels.description: The source's own missing-data codes, mapped to what each one means. IPEDS encodes three different absences as -1, -2 and -3; without this they are graded as measurements of minus one, two and three.

text_is_a_value.description: Whether a non-numeric string is the measurement rather than noise. True for URL columns.

applies_when.description: Name of an applicability predicate implemented by the reader, or null for a column that applies to every row. A name the reader does not implement is refused, never treated as 'applies to everyone'.
